_comment: Maps state -> category prefix (matching scenario id prefix like 'school-search') -> list of state-specific notes/quotes. Notes are short, user-friendly callouts shown alongside federal info.

housing.text: California landlords must give 24-hour written notice before entering (except emergencies). Security deposits are capped at 2 months unfurnished, 3 months furnished, and must be returned within 21 days.
housing.note: California has some of the strongest tenant protections in the U.S.

police.text: California law lets you refuse to show ID unless you're being arrested or driving. Police generally need a warrant to search your phone (Riley v. California also applies here).
police.note: California is a 'stop and identify' exception state — strong privacy rights.

work.text: California's minimum wage ($16+/hr statewide; higher in many cities), guaranteed paid sick leave, mandatory meal & rest breaks, and one of the strictest non-compete bans in the country.
work.note: California workers have stronger protections than federal law requires.

school.text: California explicitly protects student free speech and student journalism in public schools beyond what the federal Tinker standard requires.
school.note: California protects student speech more than the federal minimum.

housing.text: New York requires 30+ days written notice for rent increases or non-renewal (more if you've been there longer). Security deposits are capped at 1 month and must be returned within 14 days with an itemized list.
housing.note: Strong tenant protections — especially in NYC.

police.text: Under NY's 'stop and frisk' law, an officer needs reasonable suspicion of a crime to stop you. You can refuse a search and ask 'Am I free to go?'

housing.text: Texas landlords must return security deposits within 30 days. Texas allows a 3-day notice to vacate before eviction filings, which is shorter than many states.
housing.note: Texas tenant law is more landlord-friendly — know your timelines.

police.text: Texas is a 'stop and identify' state — you must give your name if lawfully arrested. You do NOT have to show ID just for being stopped (unless driving).
police.note: Know the difference between being detained and being arrested.

housing.text: Florida landlords have 15 days to return your deposit (or 30 days with a written claim). Eviction notice can be as short as 3 days for nonpayment.
housing.note: Florida timelines are tight — respond to any notice fast.

housing.text: Illinois (and especially Chicago's RLTO) requires landlords to pay interest on security deposits, give 48-hour notice before entry, and return deposits within 30-45 days.
housing.note: Chicago tenants have extra protections under the RLTO.

housing.text: Washington requires 2 days written notice before a landlord enters and 21 days to return your deposit.
housing.note: Washington is one of the more tenant-friendly states.

housing.text: Massachusetts requires landlords to hold security deposits in interest-bearing accounts and return them within 30 days. Last-month rent rules are also strict.
housing.note: MA has some of the most detailed deposit rules in the country.
